editorial.headline: Semi-Finished Metal Wholesale: Open Nationally, Barred for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This wholesale activity spans ingots to rolled steel and steel sheet, open nationally to full foreign ownership but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali under its permanent risk-based moratorium.
editorial.body:
Foreign investors cannot register PMA for this activity in Bali today. That is the decisive local fact, even though the national record marks the activity TERBUKA and sets the foreign-ownership ceiling at 100%. The Bali block follows the risk treatment applied to the listed scopes: at the Besar scale, every scope is classified in OSS as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah. Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA registration; this activity falls within that bar, recorded against the moratorium in May 2026.

The activity is wholesale trading in semi-finished metal products. It covers products of metal-ore smelting and casting, including ingots, bars, rods, billets, slabs and matte. It extends to rolled steel, tubes and pipes, profiles and hollow profiles, as well as metal powders, metal flakes and metal wire without insulation or enamel coating. The scope also expressly includes steel-sheet wholesale on one’s own account, with the cutting work ordinarily connected to that trade. Gold bullion wholesale does not form part of this activity.

Registration is open at the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. For the national foreign-investment reading, the record gives both clarity and source: TERBUKA, a maximum foreign ownership of 100%, and Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. The 100% figure is the national ceiling; it is not a Bali-specific permission. The stated scale range and national ownership position describe the activity nationally, without altering the Bali result.

That division should be read without smoothing it away. The same wholesale activity is nationally open to PMA at up to 100% foreign ownership and nevertheless unavailable for PMA registration in Bali. In the Bali record, the reason is risk-based: all of its scopes at the Besar scale sit in the Low or Medium-Low OSS categories captured by the permanent provincial moratorium. National openness is real, but it does not make a Bali PMA registration possible today.
